blocks.heading: One discipline: precise machining of heavy rotating parts
paragraphs: A locomotive wheelset, a metro bogie, a new wheel disc on a production line and a large industrial ring have something in common. Each is heavy, each turns under load, and each must be machined accurately for the system around it to run safely and efficiently.

HYT has concentrated on that problem since moving into CNC wheel lathe technology. The same engineering know-how – rigid machine structures, accurate measurement, robust CNC control and careful foundation design – serves every industry on this page. What changes is the configuration, the throughput and the way the machine fits into your workshop.

Because we design and build every machine in-house, we can adapt it to unusual wheel sizes, heavy axle loads, restricted depot space or a particular production rhythm – and we remain responsible for it after handover.

ind-railways.title: Wheel Lathes and Workshop Machines for Railways
ind-railways.description: CNC wheel lathes, wheel and axle shop machines and turnkey workshops for national railways – keeping locomotives, coaches, EMUs and wagons safe and in service.
ind-railways.lede: National railways run large, mixed fleets over long distances and heavy axle loads. HYT machines help their sheds and workshops keep every wheelset within limits without holding trains back.
ind-railways.summary: Wheel lathes, wheel shop machines and turnkey workshops for locomotive, coaching, EMU and wagon depots.

blocks.heading: Large, mixed fleets and little time to spare
paragraphs: A railway shed may maintain electric and diesel locomotives, passenger coaches, EMUs and wagons – each with its own wheel diameters, profiles and axle loads. Wheels develop flats from braking, hollow treads from wear and thin flanges on curved routes. Left uncorrected, these defects damage track, raise energy consumption and increase the risk of derailment.

Taking wheelsets out for re-profiling ties up vehicles, cranes and staff. Older wheel lathes, often decades in service, struggle to hold accuracy and are hard to keep running. Workshops need machines that restore profiles quickly, remove as little material as possible and keep working for many years.

items.q: Should a railway shed choose an underfloor or a surface wheel lathe?
items.a: An [underfloor lathe](page:underfloor-wheel-lathe) re-profiles wheels without removing the wheelset and is the right choice where vehicles must return to service quickly. A [surface wheel lathe](page:surface-wheel-lathe) suits sheds that need a flexible machine without a deep pit. We can advise on the best option for your fleet and site.

items.q: Can one machine handle locomotives, coaches and wagons?
items.a: Yes. With suitable adaptors and stored wheel profiles, one machine can serve a mixed fleet. Axle load, wheel diameter range and bogie design are confirmed during the technical study.

items.q: Can you upgrade our existing wheel lathes?
items.a: Often, yes. [Retro-fitment](page:retro-fitment-upgradation) with a new CNC system, drives and measuring equipment can restore accuracy and reliability at lower cost than a new machine.

items.q: Do you support broad, standard and metre gauge?
items.a: Our wheel lathes are configured to the customer's track gauge and wheel profiles. Gauge-dependent values are confirmed in the technical offer.

ind-metros.title: Wheel Lathes and Depot Equipment for Metros
ind-metros.description: Underfloor and tandem wheel lathes, depot equipment and maintenance contracts that help metro and rapid transit operators keep high-frequency fleets in service.
ind-metros.h1: Solutions for Metros and Rapid Transit
ind-metros.lede: Metro trains run all day and are maintained at night. HYT wheel lathes and depot equipment fit into those short windows, so the full fleet is ready for the morning peak.
ind-metros.summary: Underfloor and tandem wheel lathes and depot equipment for metro and rapid transit operators.

blocks.heading: High frequency, short windows, no spare trains
paragraphs: Metro and rapid transit fleets are sized tightly to the timetable. Frequent acceleration and braking, tight curves and high daily mileage wear wheels quickly, and ride comfort and noise are noticed immediately by passengers and neighbours.

Maintenance usually happens overnight in a depot where space is limited and every pit is planned years in advance. A wheel lathe must re-profile a whole train within that window, produce repeatable results across the fleet and be ready again the next night. When it is out of service, trains queue up and availability targets slip.

items.q: When does a metro depot need a tandem wheel lathe?
items.a: When fleets are large and maintenance windows short. A [tandem lathe](page:tandem-underfloor-wheel-lathe) machines two wheelsets of a bogie at once; HYT's YUL-12T reduces re-profiling time compared with a single machine.

items.q: Can the lathe machine brake discs as well as wheels?
items.a: Brake-disc machining is available on suitable configurations. We confirm it during the technical study of your vehicles.

items.q: How is the machine integrated into a new depot?
items.a: We supply pit, foundation and interface drawings early, coordinate with the depot designer and civil contractor, and commission the lathe on your own trains.

items.q: Can HYT operate the machine for us?
items.a: Yes. Under an [operation and maintenance](page:operation-and-maintenance) arrangement our crew runs and maintains the machine, so you can focus on running trains.

blocks.heading: Equipping a new metro depot or upgrading an existing one?
blocks.text: Share your fleet size, maintenance plan and depot layout. We will recommend the wheel lathe and depot equipment that fit your schedule.

ind-rolling-stock.title: Wheel and Axle Shop Machines for Rolling Stock OEMs
ind-rolling-stock.description: Vertical turning lathes, axle machining, wheel presses, measuring and balancing machines and wheel shop automation for rolling stock and wheelset manufacturers.
ind-rolling-stock.lede: New vehicles start with new wheelsets. HYT supplies the machines that turn, bore, press, measure and balance them – individually or as a complete, traceable wheel shop.
ind-rolling-stock.summary: Wheel and axle shop machines and automated wheel shops for rolling stock and wheelset production.

blocks.heading: Tight tolerances at production volumes
paragraphs: A rolling stock manufacturer must deliver wheelsets that meet the customer's specification first time, at the rate the assembly line demands. Bores must suit the press fit, journals must be finished for reliable bearing seats, and every wheelset must be measured, balanced and documented before it reaches the bogie.

Production programmes change: a new metro order, a different gauge, a ramp-up for an export contract. The machines in the wheel shop must adapt without long changeovers, and the data they produce must stand up to customer inspection and later warranty questions.

blocks.heading: Readiness, self-reliance and long service lives
paragraphs: Defence organisations move heavy equipment by rail and maintain their own wagons, coaches and locomotives in dedicated workshops. These fleets may run less often than commercial traffic, but they must be serviceable at short notice, and their wheelsets must meet the same safety limits as any other.

Military workshops also repair large rotating components such as rings, hubs and heavy wheels. They value equipment that is robust, simple to maintain, supported locally for decades and supplied with complete documentation. Confidentiality of drawings and site information is essential.

blocks.heading: Big parts, heavy loads, costly downtime
paragraphs: Heavy engineering works machine large rotating parts – rings, flanges, hubs, gear blanks and wheels – where size and weight make every set-up slow and every error expensive. Machines must be rigid enough to cut hard material accurately and simple enough for the shop floor to run efficiently.

Many industrial sites, such as steel plants, ports, mines and power stations, also run their own railway fleets. Their wagons and locomotives carry heavy loads on short, demanding routes, and their wheels wear quickly. Sending wheelsets away for re-profiling can stop production logistics for days.

items.q: Can HYT vertical turning lathes machine non-railway components?
items.a: Our [vertical turning and boring machines](page:vertical-turning-boring-machine) are designed for heavy rotating parts. Share your component drawings and we will confirm suitability and capacity.

items.q: We run an internal rail fleet. Do we need a full wheel shop?
items.a: Not necessarily. A [surface wheel lathe](page:surface-wheel-lathe) or [portal wheel lathe](page:portal-wheel-lathe) can give a captive fleet its own re-profiling capacity without the investment of a complete wheel shop.

items.q: Can you relocate an existing machine to a new plant?
